sources.title: Joseph J. Rotman, An Introduction to the Theory of Groups, Chapter 12: The Word Problem
sources.locator: Printed pp.418–433 (through sufficiency QED, before Cancellation Diagrams); pp.438–447 (Necessity of Boone’s Lemma through Lemma 12.15 QED). 53-page PDF starts at printed p.418.

contents.name: Introduction: fixed-presentation word problem and free-group reduction
contents.support: Fixed finite generating alphabet; inputs vary as finite signed words.

contents.name: Exercise 12.1
contents.reason: Finite-group lookup tables are already an independent decidable class; no use in the Boone construction.

contents.name: Exercise 12.2
contents.reason: Abelian normal forms supply a different decidable class; they are not used in the simulation proof.

contents.name: Exercise 12.3
contents.reason: Closure of solvable word problem under products is not needed to construct the counterexample.

contents.name: Exercise 12.4
contents.reason: Inheritance by finitely generated subgroups is not used; this proof constructs a group directly.

contents.name: Turing Machines: quadruples, instantaneous descriptions, five basic moves, terminal computations
contents.support: Normalize the local two-outcome right-infinite model explicitly, including its clamped boundary and the empty input.

contents.name: Theorem 12.1 (an r.e. nonrecursive set)
contents.support: Use the existing machine halting language, not the informal universal-machine construction in this source.

contents.name: Exercise 12.5
contents.reason: Unrecognizable subsets of the naturals are not needed; the input language here is recognizable.

contents.name: Exercise 12.6
contents.reason: The parity language is a decidable toy machine, unrelated to the required fixed undecidable recognizer.

contents.name: Exercise 12.7
contents.reason: A one-input looping example is not needed; rejecting branches are sent to an explicit loop in the compiler.

contents.name: Exercise 12.8
contents.reason: General union/intersection closure is not used by the direct computable reduction.

contents.name: Exercise 12.9
contents.reason: Boolean closure of recursive sets is replaced by composing the alleged decider with the explicit encoding.

contents.name: Exercise 12.10
contents.reason: Product encodings for arbitrary recursive subsets of naturals are not used by the fixed word compiler.

contents.name: Exercise 12.11 (one stopping state)
contents.support: Compile finite tables; map accepting to the sole stopping state and rejecting to a nonhalting loop.

contents.name: Semigroup and group solvable-word-problem definitions
contents.support: Define congruence by contextual symmetric finite derivations on nonempty words; tape contexts may be empty.

contents.name: Theorem 12.2 (identity words are r.e.)
contents.reason: Not a prerequisite for fixed undecidability. The displayed conjugate-of-products enumeration is inadequate for the full normal closure; do not import it as a proof.

contents.name: Contextual elementary operations and the presentation R(T)
contents.support: All five transition families and all three stopping cleanup families are specified.

contents.name: Lemma 12.3 (h-special preservation)
contents.support: Do not copy the false nonempty-right-tape assertion. Prove closure for augmented shapes, allowing an empty right tape in stopping state.

contents.name: Lemma 12.4 (equality to q detects computation)
contents.support: Shortest undirected path in the deterministic augmented successor graph is a forward path to q; cleanup included.

contents.name: Theorem 12.5 (Markov–Post) and Corollary 12.6
contents.support: Fix the machine and the finite presentation first; encode all input words effectively, including empty input.

contents.name: Sharp notation and special words; Boone generators and relations
contents.support: Sharp inverts each tape letter without reversing order. Presentation was checked against the page image.

contents.name: Lemma 12.7 (Boone)
contents.support: Positive special-word domain only; both directions must be proved locally.

contents.name: Theorem 12.8 (Novikov–Boone–Britton)
contents.support: Single fixed presentation with undecidable identity language; formal Turing-machine deciders.

contents.name: Corollary 12.9 (input specialization)
contents.support: Use W(h^-1 q_start v(w) h)=1. The printed corollary omits the conjugated t term and must not be copied literally.

contents.name: Lemma 12.10 (four pushing identities)
contents.support: Treat both signs of the rule letter on both sides, including empty contexts.

contents.name: Proof of sufficiency in Boone’s lemma
contents.support: Induct over symmetric semigroup histories and finish by t/k centralization.

contents.name: Lemma 12.11 (HNN tower)
contents.support: State letters are a free factor. Correct the spurious state/x commutation in part (ii-prime). Show edge bases and isomorphisms.

contents.name: Lemma 12.11, parts (iii)–(v)
contents.support: Adjoin rule letters, t, then k with explicit actual associated subgroups and injective base maps.

contents.name: Corollary 12.12 (free tape subgroups and x-inversion automorphism)
contents.support: Retraction x->1 proves free bases; the relation check gives an involutive automorphism.

contents.name: Lemma 12.13 (auxiliary equation from commutation)
contents.support: k pinch then minimal t-occurrence expression; either sign of a later t pinch reduces that expression.

contents.name: Lemma 12.14 (rule-reduced auxiliary comparisons)
contents.support: Prove associated subgroup intersection with <x> trivial; compare reduced stable-letter lengths.

contents.name: Lemma 12.15 (positive reconstruction)
contents.locator: pp.443–447, formal proof through its QED
contents.support: Preserve the stronger signed-word auxiliary induction internally; explicitly close the reverse rule orientation and empty remainders.

sources.title: Stephen G. Simpson, A Slick Proof of the Unsolvability of the Word Problem for Finitely Presented Groups (18 May 2005)
sources.locator: Complete five-page paper, Definitions 1–3 and 6, Theorems 4 and 8, Lemmas 5 and 7, Remark 9; references on p.5.

read_evidence.method: Complete web-reader text, all 262 lines including final theorem and references

contents.name: Definition 1 (HNN extension)
contents.support: Independent multi-stable-letter HNN formulation and base embedding. Translate t^-1 h t convention to the local inverse stable letter.

contents.name: Definition 2 (good subgroup)
contents.reason: Modular-machine subgroup machinery is specific to the alternate Aanderaa–Cohen proof; it is not substituted for Boone positive reconstruction.

contents.name: Definition 3 and Theorem 4 (modular machines and undecidable halting set)
contents.reason: Different machine compiler and arithmetic encoding; the assigned scope retains the explicit tape-machine/semigroup compiler.

contents.name: Lemma 5 and Definition 6 (modular subgroups and rule extension)
contents.reason: Specific subgroups of Z^2 * Z are unnecessary for the direct Boone presentation and cannot replace its associated-subgroup proof.

contents.name: Lemma 7 (halting-history generated subgroup)
contents.reason: Its modular-machine invariant is not the Boone special-word invariant required on this page.

contents.name: Theorem 8 (fixed finitely presented group with unsolvable word problem)
contents.support: Independent treatment of fixed-presentation quantifiers and commutator reduction. Mathematical cross-check, not backing for Rotman’s Lemma 12.15.

contents.name: Remark 9 (prescribed r.e. degree)
contents.reason: Exact Turing-degree realization is stronger than this fixed-undecidability endpoint and is only cited, not proved, in this paper.
